title: Medium-Term Multi-Resolution Electric Load Forecasting using Economic Data and Foundation Model (abstract page)
note: arXiv abstract page, v1 only, cs.LG, three authors (Atos, EDF R&D, LSCE, Orsay). France, forecasts 1 to 48 months ahead at monthly and daily resolution with a tabular foundation model; says selected economic covariates raise skill by 20% over 2015-2025 and MAPE stays within 4% (monthly) and 5% (daily). Text licence CC BY-NC-ND 4.0. No code link on the page.

title: Medium-Term Multi-Resolution Electric Load Forecasting (full text): design
note: Design: national French load (RTE) at daily and monthly resolution, Mar 2005 to Dec 2025. Inputs are ERA5 weather, calendar and about 40 economic series, all as observed values (hindcast); no load lags. Feature selection on 2005-2015 (10 folds, forward selection) gives 10 feature subsets whose forecasts are averaged. Rolling evaluation on 2016-2025, 85 forecasts per lead time.

title: Medium-Term Multi-Resolution Electric Load Forecasting (full text): models
note: Models: TabICLv2 (zero-shot, via the soda-inria repository; no checkpoint name, package version or hardware stated), XGBoost with default settings, and a linear model. Each is run with and without economic series in the selection pool, so the headline comparison is a model against itself with fewer inputs. Time-series foundation models are named but deliberately not used.

title: Medium-Term Multi-Resolution Electric Load Forecasting (full text): results
note: Results: daily TabICL gains about 20% at every lead time from economic inputs; monthly gain shrinks to near zero at 48 months. XGBoost: little monthly gain, clear daily gain. Linear: no daily gain. Monthly TabICL: under 1000 MW or 2% MAPE below one year, under 2000 MW or 4% beyond. Daily: under 3000 MW or 5% at 48 months for TabICL and XGBoost. Intervals are 95% bootstrap bands in figures.

title: Medium-Term Multi-Resolution Electric Load Forecasting using Economic Data and Foundation Model :: SSRN
note: SSRN posting of the same paper by the same three authors, 50 pages, posted 1 Oct 2026. A second copy of the preprint, not a peer-reviewed version and not an independent source.

title: GitHub - soda-inria/tabicl: TabICLv2: An open tabular foundation model
note: Repository of the central model. BSD 3-Clause. Default regression checkpoint is tabicl-regressor-v2-20260212.ckpt, downloaded from Hugging Face when no path is given; CPU inference is supported (thread count option). Also offers a zero-shot time-series forecaster as an optional extra. It is the model's repository, not the paper's: no analysis code for the load study.

title: tabicl on PyPI
note: Package page: tabicl 2.2.0, BSD 3-Clause, same README as the repository (v2 classifier and regressor checkpoints dated 20260212). The release date of 2.2.0 was not read from the fetched page; the research call gives 2 Sep 2026.

title: Hub record jingang/TabICL
note: Weights repository: licence bsd-3-clause, not gated, created 12 Feb 2026, head 4dcd344 (18 Feb 2026). Files include tabicl-regressor-v2-20260212.ckpt and three classifier checkpoints. Repository name was found by a direct fetch; the file names match those in the TabICL README.

title: Commit history jingang/TabICL
note: Four commits: the checkpoints were uploaded on 12 Feb 2026 (commit d700cf0, four files); the two later commits (12 and 18 Feb 2026) are README edits by title. 12 Feb 2026 is inside our scored window; 38 of the 52 scored weeks start after it.

title: Research call: code, data, pre-registration, replication (nothing found)
note: One standard research call (LinkedIn excluded) reported no paper-specific GitHub, Zenodo or Hugging Face record, no pre-registration and no independent replication, criticism or follow-up. Its other sources were the arXiv and SSRN records, the TabICL repository, releases and PyPI pages, two aggregator pages repeating the abstract, and TabPFN pages that do not concern this study.

title: Medium-Term Multi-Resolution Electric Load Forecasting (full text): caveats and appendices
note: Authors' caveats: errors use observed inputs and would be larger operationally; models disagree on which economic series matter; the selection step is debatable. Appendix: without selection daily TabICL RMSE reaches 5000 MW against 3000 MW; 70-90% of the context costs about 10% error. The data link's target was lost in extraction; no code statement.
